Induce a drift in a benchmark source

Source: R/dsg_benchmark.R
dsg_drift.Rd

Moves a dsg_source() to another concept and verifies the drift: a virtual drift must make the kernel two-sample test (dsg_mmd_test()) reject at virtual_p_value, and a real drift must change at least real_drift_level of the labels of the same points. Candidates that fail are discarded; after max_tries candidates, the strongest real drift found is used with a warning.

Usage

dsg_drift(source, type = "a")

Arguments

source

dsg_source object

type

"-" (or "_") no drift, "v" pure virtual drift, "r" pure real drift, "c" both, "a" any of them.

Value

list with the updated source, the logical flags virtual and real, and the verification statistics p_value (two-sample test, NA without virtual drift) and label_change (share of changed labels, NA without real drift)

Examples

set.seed(2)
drift <- dsg_drift(dsg_sine(), "r")
drift$real
#> [1] TRUE
drift$label_change
#> [1] 0.748
